title: Willem Janszoon makes the first recorded European landing in Australia
summary: The Dutch ship Duyfken under Willem Janszoon landed at the Pennefather River on the Cape York Peninsula, the first documented European landing on Australia.
reason: The Dutch East India Company sent Janszoon from Banten to search for trade opportunities around New Guinea.
significance: It began European contact with the Australian continent.
place: Pennefather River, Cape York Peninsula, Australia
